newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada secondary offering completed.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada secondary offering completed.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Thursday it completed a secondary offering of its stock but shelved a related primary offering.
Gulf Canada said the secondary offering totaled 18.2 million of its ordinary shares previously held by major stockholders at US$8.125 each.
The number of shares sold was below the 20.1 million spelled out in a June 25 preliminary prospectus.
The company also decided not to sell 4 million treasury shares as part of the deal, Gulf spokesman Dennis Martin said in a telephone interview from Denver.
"Based on the offering price, Gulf elected not to sell any primary shares in the offering," Martin said.
The moves meant Gulf Canada's public float rose to 68 percent from the previous 61 percent and total outstanding shares remain at 269 million, he said.

Of the 18.2 million shares in the secondary offering, 16.2 million were sold by A&G Resources, a group of banks, and 1.96 million were sold by two members of a group that invested C$300 million in Gulf in 1995, kicking off its restructuring.
Those included Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board and University of Chicago.
With the deal's completion, A&G's stake in Gulf is now 19 percent and the Torch Energy Advisers-led group of institutions' interest is 13 percent.
Gulf shares in Toronto were up 0.25 on Thursday to 11.50 in moderate volume of 158,411 shares.

In New York, the company's American Depositary Receipts were among the New York Stock Exchange's most active issues, climbing 3/16 to 8-3/8 with nearly 2.1 million changing hands. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
